reference: Installed hostname for plain gethostname and short-name reads in the same isolated UTS environment; documented read-only fixture hooks for full/short/domain and token rendering. Fixture contracts do not claim DNS, interface discovery or GNU -f parity.
coverage: The hostname command is registered as a Bash builtin.
Bash help exposes the documented hostname forms and their key read-mode contract.
Deferred plans cover name formatting, address discovery, positional and file-based setting, dry-run behavior, and argument validation.
Operation coverage: isolated plain/short hostname reads, dotted and undotted fixture formatting, and fixture-only IP/FQDN token rendering.
Exact dry-run audit for positional and CRLF relative-file names plus unchanged observed hostname; syscall-count proof remains deferred.
exclusions: Setting the UTS hostname remains deferred. Live address discovery remains deferred because it can use resolver/network interfaces.
Read-only fixture hooks are custom contracts; no live DNS or interface behavior is inferred.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Verify through Bash's type builtin that the catalogued hostname command is registered as a shell builtin, not resolved from PATH.
Check that Bash help publishes the implementation's documented hostname forms, option exclusivity, and fixture hook without invoking hostname itself.
cases.script:
h=$(help hostname)
[[ $h == *"Get or set the system hostname."* ]]
[[ $h == *"bashhostname -s"* ]]
[[ $h == *"-s, -d, -f, -i, -I, -A are mutually exclusive."* ]]
[[ $h == *"BASHOS_HOSTNAME_FIXTURE_ROOT"* ]]
printf 'hostname help contract
'

cases.purpose: Render dotted and undotted names from the documented read-only fixture hook, including CRLF trimming and an empty domain.
cases.script:
mkdir fixture
export BASHOS_HOSTNAME_FIXTURE_ROOT=fixture
printf 'node.fixture.test\r\n' > fixture/hostname
hostname
hostname -f
hostname -s
hostname -d
printf 'plain\n' > fixture/hostname
hostname -s
hostname -d

cases.purpose: Check -i, -I, and -A formatting, token order, duplicate handling, and empty-result behavior with deterministic resolver and interface data.
cases.reason: Live resolver and interface discovery requires a future disposable VM with reviewed resolver/getifaddrs mocks and independent expected discovery results. The runnable text-file hooks cover rendering only and do not establish live discovery or deduplication behavior.

cases.purpose: Exercise positional hostname setting, successful isolated state change, and rejection of names at the length and slash boundaries.
cases.reason: The positional form calls sethostname(2) and changes kernel UTS state. It needs a disposable VM with a private UTS namespace and the narrowly required capability, or a reviewed syscall mock that records arguments and returns controlled results; the host or ordinary candidate runner must not be used.

cases.purpose: Exercise -F with a small relative fixture containing a newline or CRLF, and cover empty and unreadable-file errors without host paths.
cases.reason: A successful -F operation also calls sethostname(2). A future disposable private-UTS VM or reviewed syscall mock must accept only relative files inside its private fixture tree and record the exact name passed to the syscall; no host path may be used.

cases.purpose: The documented dry-run branches render positional and relative CRLF-file names without changing the hostname; independent audit bytes are exact.
cases.script:
before=$(hostname)
hostname -n fixture.test
printf 'file.fixture.test\r\n' > name
hostname --dry-run -F name
[[ $(hostname) == "$before" ]]
cases.stderr_text:
bashhostname: dry-run: would set hostname to 'fixture.test'
bashhostname: dry-run: would set hostname to 'file.fixture.test'

cases.purpose: Conflicting print selectors and a missing -F operand fail in argument parsing before any hostname-setting syscall.
cases.script:
for scenario in selectors missing-file; do
 rc=0
 case $scenario in
 selectors) hostname -s -d || rc=$? ;;
 missing-file) hostname -F || rc=$? ;;
 esac
 [[ $rc == 2 ]]
 printf '%s=%s\n' "$scenario" "$rc"
done

cases.purpose: Read the isolated kernel hostname and short form without changing it or performing resolution.
The documented read-only hooks render supplied token order and duplicates; they do not exercise discovery or deduplication.
cases.script:
mkdir fixture
export BASHOS_HOSTNAME_FIXTURE_ROOT=fixture
printf '192.0.2.7\t2001:db8::7 192.0.2.7\n' > fixture/ipaddrs
printf '198.51.100.9\n' > fixture/ifaddrs
printf 'a.fixture.test\tb.fixture.test\n' > fixture/fqdns
hostname -i
hostname -I
hostname -A
: > fixture/ipaddrs
hostname -i

cases.purpose: Prove no sethostname syscall is issued by any dry-run form, beyond checking the documented output and unchanged observed name.
cases.reason: Requires a future reviewed sethostname syscall counter/mock in a disposable VM. The current byte/audit contract cannot observe attempted syscalls; no UTS mutation is authorized.
